 Martinez Property Owners Face Dec. 10 Tax Payment Deadline
 The first installment of Contra Costa County secured property taxes must be paid by 5 p.m. to avoid a 10% penalty.
 Patch News , Patch Staff 
 Posted Tue, Nov 17, 2026 at 8:44 am PT Martinez property owners must pay the first installment of their 2026-27 secured property taxes by 5 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 10, to avoid a 10% penalty. The Contra Costa County Treasurer-Tax Collector’s Office offers online, phone, mail, in-person and drop-box payment options.
 The first installment was due Sunday, Nov. 1. Owners who had not received a bill by that date should call 925-608-9500. Not receiving a bill does not excuse late payment.
 Owners can pay through the Tax Portal or call the automated payment system at 925-608-9500. PayPal, credit card and debit card payments carry a 2.5% service fee, with a $3.50 minimum. E-checks have no service fee, but rejected e-checks can incur a returned-check fee of up to $85.

 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . Checks with installment coupons can be mailed to P.O. Box 51104, Los Angeles, CA 90051, using the provided envelope. Mailed payments need a USPS postmark before the delinquency date to avoid penalties. Owners paying both installments together must include both coupons.
 In-person payments are accepted at the Contra Costa County Finance Building, 625 Court St., Suite 100, Martinez, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Monday through Friday, excluding holidays. A drive-thru check drop box on the building’s Main Street side is available 24 hours daily but closes at 5 p.m. Thursday, Dec. 10.

 Subscribe By subscribing, you agree to Patch's Privacy Policy and Terms of Use . The second installment is due Monday, Feb. 1, 2027. Its listed delinquency date, Saturday, April 10, moves to 5 p.m. Monday, April 12, under the county’s next-business-day rule. Late second-installment payments incur a 10% penalty and $20 administrative charge.
 Owners can also sign up for paperless billing for email reminders and secure access. Participants receive their tax bills at their registered email addresses.
